title: Fairmont Senior's Brylee Stevens and Beatrice Clevenger sign letters of intent | Fairmont Sports | wvnews.com
text:
FAIRMONT, W.Va. — Fairmont Senior’s Brylee Stevens and Beatrice Clevenger each made it official where they will be continuing their academic and athletic careers.
On Wednesday, Stevens, joined by her family, coach and teammates, signed her national letter of intent to join the women’s lacrosse team at Bethany College.
Also on Wednesday, Clevenger, joined by her parents who are also her coaches as well as classmates and teammates, will stay local as she signed her national letter of intent to join the women’s swim team at Fairmont State University.
Stevens began playing lacrosse as a sophomore and quickly improved to the point that she will be continuing to play the game at the next level.
“I chose Bethany (College) because I really enjoyed playing lacrosse my three years that I started,” Stevens said. “I grew (my skills with) more than just a team, I grew (into) a family and I wanted a chance play with my best friend Hayden (Chickerell) again.”
While Stevens did consider another school, she instantly knew it was the place for her.
“There was one other school I looked at,” Stevens said. “It didn’t end up being a fit for me, but I just knew when I went to Bethany (College), it was home.”
Like at Fairmont Senior, she will play a defensive position for the Bison.
Stevens is planning to study nursing.
“My youngest brother is a diabetic, and I grew up taking care of him,” Stevens said. “I (thought it was) something that I really liked doing, and I decided to make a career out of it.”
Clevenger chose Fairmont State for a number of reasons — mainly the members of the team and the coach that she is already well acquainted with.
“I have a lot of old teammates (at Fairmont State) from club (swim), and I’m really close with the coach, so I really enjoy all the people in it,” Clevenger said.
It was the only college she considered attending, and she will not be far from her friends or family.
“I just wanted to stay home, close to my friends and my family to stay close (with them),” Clevenger said.
Clevenger said she intends to compete in multiple events for the Fighting Falcons, mainly longer-distance events.
“I plan on doing the longer distance events, so 200 or 500 freestyle,” Clevenger said.
She is planning to study exercise physiology.
“I want to be a PT or athletic trainer,” Clevenger said. “I dealt with an injury this year, so just wanting to help people like me.”
